What this release changes - and what this receipt accepts - is the macOS documentation a reader executes.

clean_host.note: Mac: the owner's OMP client, launcher, agent configuration and sessions moved aside; the release cloned at the reader's path (~/omp-ninfer); the only inherited state was the operator's SSH identity for the destination, which the route requires a reader to have

documented_blocks_verbatim.note: every executed step's bytes hashed to the documented block's SHA-256 recorded in the bundle manifest; the only substitution is USER@RUNTIME_HOST -> the operator's destination, which is the reader's own value

tunnel_semantics.note: the tunnel block ran in the background where the prose says 'in another terminal', the runner waited for the local port, and stopped the exec'd ssh - not just its wrapper - before the fail-closed block where the prose says Ctrl-C

system_python.note: the runner and every block ran on macOS's system python3 (3.9.6), the only Python a stranger has

windows_destination.note: the key-copy and restart blocks were executed against a Windows OpenSSH destination whose default shell is cmd.exe; both forms were also measured byte-identical on a Linux destination

complete_run.note: a run that executes fewer steps than the bundle lists is a failure; run 6 of this window was exactly that false pass and is now a regression test

hosts_restored.note: Mac: the owner's ~/.omp/agent, launcher, and client restored; the reader-path clone removed. RTX 5090 appliance: production container serving (restarted once by the route's survives-restart block, as documented), health ok, port and restart policy unchanged.
